verdicts.trueWording: the official census of 50.000 was taken 15 years ago
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched by curl (browser UA, HTTP 200). Quote is verbatim in the 'Gaz 1 Part 4: The Lay of the Land' post, subheading 'An Array of Strange Places'. Every limb holds: GAZ1, Specularum, official census of 50.000, taken 15 years ago; page adds it has grown considerably since.

Raw page, same Gaz 1 Part 4 post, paragraph immediately after the Specularum passage: the other notable places in Karameikos get their own descriptions, some merit only a paragraph. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: His prose is dispassionate, methodical, and encouraging
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched by curl (HTTP 200). Verbatim in the section 'The Translotar: J. Eric Holmes and the Bridge Between Worlds'; the surrounding sentences name Holmes and the Holmes Basic Set, so the prose attribution holds.

verdicts.trueWording: The text in the set was dense and peculiar
verdicts.note: The quotation is verbatim in the Holmes section, but the essay never dates the original boxed set: it says only 'the original boxed set', and the sole years it prints are 1930, 1977, 1970, 1948, 1981 and 1980. The 1974 date is the claim's own gloss, not the page's, so the attribution 'the same essay calls the original 1974 boxed set' overstates what is on the page.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the 1974 dating of the boxed set

verdicts.trueWording: Moldvay's text seems both efficient and lyrical
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'The poet: Tom Moldvay and the Art of Elegance'. The 1981 limb is supported in the same paragraph, which dates the Basic D&D set to 1981.

verdicts.trueWording: Each adventure implied a cosmology, a history, and a mood
verdicts.note: Raw page, Moldvay section, paragraph on Isle of Dread and The Lost City. The page continues that the mood was built in by its placement of statues, monsters and ruins, supporting that limb too.

verdicts.trueWording: These adventures communicated worldviews, rather than merely offering maps
verdicts.note: Raw page, Moldvay section, the sentence immediately preceding the cosmology sentence; refers to Isle of Dread and The Lost City.

verdicts.trueWording: His settlement populations and locations followed real-world economic maxims
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched by curl (HTTP 200), byline John Roy, Oct 21 2024. Verbatim as the opening sentence of the second paragraph under the heading 'Keeping It Real'; the preceding sentence names Gygax, so 'His' is Gygax.

verdicts.trueWording: each nation's imports and exports and the trade routes they used
verdicts.note: Raw page, same 'Keeping It Real' paragraph: he provided each nation's imports and exports and the trade routes they used to transport them. Subject is Gygax, named in the same paragraph.

verdicts.trueWording: We made no more than what we could put on a page
verdicts.note: Raw transcript fetched by curl (HTTP 200), part 1, dated July 14 2025. Verbatim at the end of Zeb Cook's first answer in the exchange on models of world building, which opens 'when we started doing things [at TSR], we were doing modules'. TSR and the early-module limbs are both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: For every module, you had to create a quick setting
verdicts.note: Raw transcript, part 1, same Zeb Cook turn; the page continues 'so you could explain it', supporting the purpose limb.

verdicts.trueWording: You obviously have a whole bunch more
verdicts.note: Raw transcript, part 1, the paragraph after the page remark: 'Then we got letters from people saying...' followed by 'No, we don't have anything more on that.' Readers writing in and the belief in more material are both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: The Forgotten Realms is the kitchen sink approach to world building
verdicts.note: Raw transcript, part 1, verbatim in Wolfgang Baur's turn replying to Cook on the TSR settings; the turn is speaker-tagged 'Wolfgang' and the seminar intro identifies him as Wolfgang Baur of Kobold Press.

verdicts.trueWording: to provide the minimum viable world building
verdicts.note: Raw transcript, part 1, Baur's turn: a new model of world building that Kobold Press and others have pursued, which is to provide the minimum viable world building; the next sentence names the one-book model.

verdicts.trueWording: are ones that are literally just lists of places and people
verdicts.note: Raw transcript fetched by curl (HTTP 200), part 2, dated July 21 2025, in the exchange on conflict. The paragraph is an unbroken continuation of the turn tagged 'Zeb:' ('Yeah, there's conflict there'), with the next speaker tag being 'Wolfgang:' two paragraphs later, so the attribution to Cook holds.
